PullRequest.Title: agentHost: preserve peer checkpoints after host notices
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
Fixes a regression introduced by #334301: an Agent Merge host notice updates the default chat's modification time without capturing a checkpoint, allowing its older checkpoint to hide newer peer-chat edits in Session Changes.

- Rank each chat's last attributable completed turn by `startedAt + duration`, using the existing timestamp helper.
- Preserve host-notice filtering and the existing fallback for restored turns without timing data.
- Add two-chat tests verifying that a host notice preserves the peer checkpoint and both edits, while a genuinely newer Agent Merge repair turn becomes the endpoint.

## Validation
- Proved the notice regression fails with the original selection logic: it selects `main-checkpoint` and omits file B.
- `npm run transpile-client` passed.
- Targeted hygiene/ESLint passed for both changed files.
- `node test\unit\node\index.js --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostChangesetService.test.ts`: **31 passing, 37 pre-existing skipped**.

Host-service tests use the production state manager; no Electron/UI validation was run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh a multi-chat Session Changes changeset after a hidden host-notice turn completes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Turn completion schedules the session recompute fire-and-forget, so it is off the agent turn's completion critical path; an observing Session Changes client waits for the per-session sequencer, checkpoint lookup, Git diff, publication, and persistence before the refreshed file list is ready.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the session database for the static changeset computation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session DB open per queued session recompute.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same DB open occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the session changeset compute can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two checkpoint lookups issued in parallel per Git-backed session recompute, independent of chat count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two checkpoint lookups occurred; only the selected turn ID changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both must complete before the Git diff starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute file diffs between the baseline and selected checkpoint refs through the Git service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Git diff per session recompute; no per-chat fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One Git diff was already performed per recompute, previously against the last attributable turn of the most-recently-modified chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks publication of the refreshed Session Changes contents.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and persist the computed diff list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full diff-list serialization/persist per successful recompute.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same serialization and persistence occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after publication and does not determine the in-memory ready state.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The in-memory selector visits each chat and scans backward only over its trailing host-notice turns; effective work is O(chat count plus trailing notices), while downstream boundary cardinality remains one grouped session computation. Typical turns stop at the first attributable tail turn.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refreshes are serialized by the per-session, per-kind sequencer. The two checkpoint lookups run in parallel, followed by one Git diff; the change adds no concurrency or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Checkpoint selection is recomputed from in-memory state on every queued refresh. Persisted changeset data can seed restored UI, but successful refreshes still perform checkpoint resolution and a Git diff; the diff does not alter cache keys or cold/warm behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed selector, sequencer, checkpoint calls, and Git boundary are directly traced. It retains the prior reverse-turn scan complexity and adds only one timestamp conversion per chat.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Chat counts and notice-tail lengths vary, but the added Date conversion is bounded by chat count and is dominated by the unchanged checkpoint/Git work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff changes which existing checkpoint lookup and single Git diff are used; it neither adds a boundary nor increases boundary cardinality. The per-chat timestamp conversion is minor bounded CPU work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh Session Changes after a genuine newer peer or Agent Merge repair turn
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For turn-complete refreshes, recomputation is queued asynchronously and does not delay turn completion; the Session Changes view waits for the queued DB/checkpoint/Git pipeline. Initial subscription likewise waits for this pipeline to populate fresh state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open per queued session recompute.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read baseline and selected-turn checkpoint refs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two parallel lookups per recompute, not per chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unchanged cardinality; the selector can now choose a different turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes and gates Git diff computation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Diff the baseline against the selected latest completed turn checkpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Git diff per recompute after all chats are grouped into one selected endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One Git diff was already issued against the chat chosen by modifiedAt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the refreshed view's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chats and trailing hidden notices controls selector CPU; repository change size controls the unchanged Git diff and result serialization. There is no per-chat Git or checkpoint fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-session session-changeset recomputes are serialized. Checkpoint reads are parallelized as before, and only one Git operation runs for this scenario.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The previous file list remains visible while recomputation runs and successful results are persisted. Endpoint selection itself is not cached, but prior code also rescanned each chat's turns; restored turns without timing data use the existing chat modifiedAt value.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: added code performs one Date parse/format per chat after the same reverse attributable-turn search and feeds the same single-checkpoint pipeline.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large chat catalogs could increase timestamp-conversion CPU linearly, but realistic cardinality and the unchanged dominant Git operation make user-visible degradation unsupported.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. Before and after perform one grouped session Git diff, and the changed work is bounded in-memory ordering logic rather than new I/O, retention, eager initialization, or concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and traced session refresh triggers, sequencing, checkpoint resolution, Git computation, fallback/persistence, turn-history scaling, and tests. No diff-introduced actionable performance regression was found; the change preserves existing scan complexity and expensive-boundary cardinality while correcting checkpoint ordering.
